## Code Library Loading
This code loads the libraries required to perform this model simulation. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Set Seed for Randomization

```{r}
set.seed(10)
samplesize <- 1000
nitems <- 5
```

## Data Generation
This is a small scale example of the basic steps needed for model generation.

This code creates the matrix that will be used to store our simulation data

```{r}
sim_matrix <- matrix(NA,
                      ncol = 1+nitems,
              nrow = samplesize)
col_names <- c("Class")

col_names <- append(col_names,paste0("Item_", 1:5))

colnames(sim_matrix) <- col_names

print(sim_matrix)
```

This code determines the membership probability vector.
```{r}
##class membership probability vector
pop_distribution_classes <- c(.2, .1, .4, .3)
print(cumsum(pop_distribution_classes))
```
This helps determine group membership. For example,a point with class distribution number 0.4 would be put in class 3. 

```{r}
for (i in 1:samplesize) {
  tmp1 <- runif(n=1)
###   print(tmp1)
  class <- match(TRUE, tmp1 < cumsum(pop_distribution_classes))

  observation_data <- runif(n = 5)
  
  for ( x in 1:length(observation_data)){
  if (observation_data[x] < population_response_probability_model[class, x]){
    observation_data_coded[x] = 1
  } else {
    observation_data_coded[x] = 2
  }
}

sim_matrix[i, ] <- c(class, observation_data_coded)
### print(simdata.mat)
}

head(sim_matrix)
```

## Code chunk break down
This code randomly generates a number for a data point (tmp1) that determines class membership.
```{r}
#random generation for tmp1 membership
tmp1 <- runif(n=1)
print(tmp1)
```
This code determines which class the point would fall into.
```{r}
#determines class membership
class <- match(TRUE, tmp1 < cumsum(pop_distribution_classes))
print(class)
```
This is the response probability matrix. The rows are the classes, and the columns are used to determin tmp1's response data.
```{r}
## Response Probability Matrix
population_response_probability_model <- rbind(rep(0.9, 5), c(rep(0.1, 2), rep(0.9, 2)),c(rep(0.9, 3), rep(0.1, 3)), rep(0.1,5))
print(population_response_probability_model)
```

This randomly generates numbers to create the item response for tmp1.
```{r}
#generating random data for tmp1 data point
observation_probabilities <- runif(5)
print(observation_probabilities)
```
This code determines the exact responses for the tmp1. This is done by comparing the class response probability with the randomly generated observation data. For example, if a datapoint was put in class 4, you would only compare with the 4th row of the response probability matrix. The final observational_data_coded represents tmp1's item responses in this simulation.
```{r}

observation_data <- rep(0,5)

for ( x in 1:length(observation_probabilities)){
  if (observation_probabilities[x] < population_response_probability_model[class, x]){
    observation_data_coded[x] = 1
  } else {
    observation_data_coded[x] = 2
  }
}

print(observation_data_coded)
```
